faq: Which help desks can you sort tickets in?
Zendesk, Freshdesk, Help Scout, Gorgias, Intercom and shared Gmail or Outlook inboxes are all common. If yours has labels and an API or rules engine, it usually works.
How do you decide the tags?
We read a sample of your tickets, propose a short tag list and agree it with you. Fewer clear tags work better than a long list nobody remembers.
What happens to tickets it cannot classify?
They are tagged needs review and land in a general queue, so nothing is hidden. We watch how many fall there during testing and adjust.
Does it read private customer details?
It reads the ticket text to choose a tag. We pick tools with suitable data terms and tell you where processing happens. Tell us if some topics must stay out of it.

desc:
AI ticket sorting by topic and urgency makes sure the right person sees the right message first. Ecom Swift LLC adds automatic tagging to your help desk, so each new ticket receives a topic, an urgency level and a language label within moments.

## What is AI ticket sorting?

AI ticket sorting reads each new support ticket and attaches labels: what the message is about, how urgent it is and which language it is written in. Rules you define then place the ticket in the right queue or assign it to the right person. You choose the labels and can see why a tag was chosen.

## Why unsorted queues hide the urgent cases

In a plain inbox, every message looks alike. A customer reporting a missing parcel sits beside a newsletter reply and a supplier pitch. Agents scan subject lines, open tickets in order of arrival and sometimes find the angry customer hours later.

Manual sorting by a person does not scale either. It takes time, depends on who is on shift and tends to be dropped when the day gets busy. Missing labels also make later reporting unreliable.

## How sorting improves speed and focus

Sorting moves work to the right hands without a person acting as a switchboard. Billing questions go to billing, delivery questions go to the fulfilment contact and a customer writing in German reaches a colleague who speaks it. Each agent works inside their strength, which speeds up replies.

Urgency tags matter most. When a message mentions a chargeback, a safety concern or a loud complaint, it rises to the top of the queue. Tags also create clean counts, so you can see how many tickets each topic generates.

## What a good sorting setup includes

- A short list of topic tags that fit your business.
- Urgency levels, such as low, normal and high.
- Language detection written into a tag.
- Routing rules that send tickets to queues or named people.
- Escalation for angry customers or valued accounts.
- A fallback tag for messages the system cannot classify.
- A test on a batch of your past tickets to check accuracy.
- An explanation of why each tag was chosen, available to your team.
- A weekly count of tickets by topic.
- A short guide to your tags for new staff.

## How we work

We start by reading a sample of your tickets and proposing tags. You approve, merge or rename them, because the labels must make sense to your team. We then connect the tagging to your help desk or inbox with limited access, set the routing rules and test on past tickets, comparing the tags with what an agent would have chosen.

The Basic package adds topic tags to one help desk. The Standard package adds urgency, language and routing to several queues, tested on a larger set. The Premium package widens the tag list, adds escalation rules, routes to more queues, supplies a weekly topic count and a tag guide. Tickets that cannot be classified are never lost. They go to a general queue for a person.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep tags few and clearly named.
- Decide what makes a ticket urgent in your business.
- Review a sample of tagged tickets every week.
- Remove tags nobody uses.

**Avoid:**
- Creating a tag for every rare case.
- Overlapping tags that mean nearly the same thing.
- Routing automatically before the tags have been tested.
- Hiding the reason for a tag from your agents.
- Forgetting a queue for unclear messages.

## Who this is for

A growing store whose shared inbox is too busy for one person to triage. A support team spread across languages or time zones. A business that wants dependable topic counts for planning.

## What we need from you

Access to your help desk or inbox as an admin, agent or collaborator, never a password, and a short list of how your team is organized. Tell us which customers or topics deserve fast treatment. Any existing tags are welcome, and we can tidy them if you add the tag cleanup.
